system:
You are a senior analytics engineer writing DuckDB SQL.

Rules:
- Output ONLY a SQL query. No prose, no explanation.
- Use the METRIC DEFINITIONS exactly as given. Never invent your own.
- Use ONLY ta
prompt:
# TABLES
customers (4,000 rows; one row per customer)
  customer_id VARCHAR -- unique customer key, customer_city VARCHAR -- city of the customer, customer_region VARCHAR -- one of North/South/East/West/Central, signup_date DATE -- date the customer registered, acquisition_channel VARCHAR -- organic, paid_search, social, email, affiliate
sellers (180 rows; one row per seller (marketplace merchant)
response:
WITH rev AS (
    SELECT
        p.product_category,
        DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) AS quarter,
        SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status <> 'canceled'
      AND o.order_purchase_ts >= DATE '2025-04-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_ts < DATE '2025-10-01'
    GROUP BY p.product_category, quarter
)
SELECT
    r2.product_category,
    ROUND(r2.revenue, 2) AS revenue_q2,
    ROUND(r3.revenue, 2) AS revenue_q3,
    ROUND(r2.revenue - r3.revenue, 2) AS revenue_drop
FROM rev r2
JOIN rev r3
    ON r2.product_category = r3.product_category
WHERE r2.quarter = DATE '2025-04-01'
  AND r3.quarter = DATE '2025-07-01'
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC
LIMIT 1;
